samples.summary: Remote-peer presence fields (now including `lineAffinity` on `activeCursorPos`) are consumed without any runtime validation at the trust boundary
samples.evidence: `DocsPresence` in packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:21-40 is only a TypeScript type; the values arrive over Yorkie from other clients and are attacker-controllable by any peer with edit/view access to the document. `buildPeerCursors` (docs-view.tsx:219-234) forwards `p.presence.activeCursorPos` and `p.presence.activeSelection.{anchor,focus}` straight into `PeerCursor.position` / `.selection`, which reach `resolvePositionPixel` (packages/docs/src/view/peer-cursor.ts:97) and `computeSelectionRects` (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:547). This delta widens that wire shape by typing `lineAffinity` on `activeCursorPos`. I traced the consumers and could NOT find an exploitable outcome: the affinity is only compared against the literal `'forward'` (peer-cursor.ts:199), a non-string value simply falls back to backward; offsets are used in bounded loops over layout lines and end in canvas `fillRect`/`fillText`, not innerHTML (grep for dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML under packages/frontend/src/app/docs returned nothing). So the impact I can substantiate is only cosmetic mis-rendering, not a crash or injection. Reporting as hardening: a peer-supplied field crossing into render math with no allow-list check is the kind of boundary that becomes a liability as more fields ride along on it (a validating shim at getPresences()/buildPeerCursors would fix the whole class).
